An atomic unit of healthcare data exchange in FHIR (Patient, Encounter, Observation, etc.). Each resource has a stable id, a versionable meta block, and a JSON or XML serialisation defined by the FHIR specification.
A FHIR container resource that groups other resources for transmission as a single unit. Bundle types include searchset (search results), transaction (atomic write), and document (clinical document).

FHIR resource that represents an interaction between a patient and a healthcare provider — inpatient stay, outpatient visit, emergency contact. Anchors clinical observations and procedures to a specific care episode.
FHIR resource for measurements and simple assertions about a patient — vital signs, lab results, social history. Components carry coded result values typed via UCUM units and LOINC codes.
FHIR resource representing an order or prescription for a medication. Carries medication coding (typically RxNorm), dosage instructions, and intent (order, plan, proposal).

ONC-defined minimum set of data classes and elements that certified EHRs must support for interoperable exchange. Versioned annually; v3 added social determinants of health and clinical notes elements.
aliases: United States Core Data for Interoperability

extras.definition: Universal coding system for laboratory and clinical observations maintained by the Regenstrief Institute. Required by USCDI for lab results and many vital sign panels.
aliases: Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes

extras.definition: Normalised naming system for clinical drugs maintained by the U.S. National Library of Medicine. Provides stable concept identifiers (RXCUIs) for medication coding in FHIR MedicationRequest and prescription workflows.
U.S. clinical modification of WHO ICD-10 used for diagnosis coding on claims and clinical documentation. Roughly 70,000 codes covering disease, injury, and external cause classifications.
Comprehensive clinical terminology covering findings, procedures, and observable entities. Required by USCDI for problem list and encounter type coding; richer than ICD for clinical decision support.
aliases: Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine — Clinical Terms

extras.definition: A pointer from one FHIR resource to another, expressed as a relative URL like Patient/123 or an absolute URL. Enables the resource graph that ties Observations to Encounters to Patients.
A FHIR terminology resource enumerating the codes drawn from one or more CodeSystems that may be used in a specific binding. Used to constrain coded fields in profiles and forms.
A FHIR terminology resource that defines the concepts (codes, displays, hierarchies) of a code system such as LOINC or SNOMED CT. Distinguished from a ValueSet, which selects from CodeSystems.

FIX message that carries a single order from a buy-side firm to a broker or venue. Identifies the instrument, side, quantity, order type, and time-in-force; typically the first message in an order's life cycle.

FIX message a venue or broker sends to acknowledge, fill, partially fill, replace, cancel, or reject an order. The execution life cycle of every FIX order is told through a stream of ExecutionReports.

FIX message that delivers a full snapshot of the current state of a market data subscription — top-of-book or depth-of-book — at a point in time. Contrast with MarketDataIncrementalRefresh for tick-by-tick updates.
A numeric field identifier in a FIX message body, e.g. 35=MsgType, 55=Symbol, 38=OrderQty. Tag-value pairs are SOH-delimited; the schema is versioned by FIX protocol release (4.4, 5.0 SP2, FIXT).
FIX message used to report a trade between counterparties to a venue or central matching service. Drives downstream affirmation, allocation, and settlement workflows.

An XML representation of an OTC derivative trade — IRS, CDS, FX option — defined by ISDA's FpML standard. Carries economic terms in product-specific blocks and is widely used in SEF and DTCC reporting.
Concrete decision binding an order_line to a fulfillment node and decrementing the corresponding ATP. Issued by the DOM broker after sourcing-rule scoring; reversible up to the pick_started event.

A logically continuous, sequenced bidirectional conversation between two FIX endpoints, identified by SenderCompID/TargetCompID. Sessions handle Logon, Logout, Heartbeat, ResendRequest, and SequenceReset administrative traffic.
A read-only, real-time FIX feed of executions sent to a third party — typically a clearing broker, risk system, or compliance group — for shadow position keeping and surveillance.

A standardised schema and vocabulary that lets researchers run identical analyses across heterogeneous data sources. OMOP, PCORnet, and Sentinel are the dominant CDMs in observational health research.
A row in the OMOP CONCEPT table representing a single clinical idea — a drug, condition, procedure, or measurement — identified by a stable concept_id and tied to a Vocabulary and Domain.
An OMOP-defined clinical area (Drug, Condition, Procedure, Measurement, Observation, Device) that determines which CDM table a Concept belongs in. Domain-routing is the first step in ETL into OMOP.
A coded terminology managed within OMOP — SNOMED, RxNorm, LOINC, ICD-10-CM, NDC, etc. The Vocabulary tables define concept ids, hierarchies, and concept-to-concept relationships.

The canonical concept that OMOP-standardised analytics build on — typically SNOMED for conditions, RxNorm for drugs, LOINC for measurements. Source codes are mapped to a Standard Concept via concept_relationship.
The original code from the source system (ICD-9-CM, NDC, local lab codes) preserved alongside the Standard Concept after ETL. Lets researchers audit and re-map without losing fidelity.
A reusable specification of a patient population — entry events, inclusion criteria, exit rules — typically authored in ATLAS and exported as a JSON definition or generated SQL.
OHDSI's open-source web application for browsing OMOP vocabularies, designing cohort definitions, characterising populations, and generating analytic SQL against a CDM database.

Federated observational studies executed by sites in the Observational Health Data Sciences and Informatics network, each running the same analytic package against their local OMOP CDM and contributing only aggregate results.
An OMOP CDM concept representing a span of time during which a person's clinical events would have been recorded. Critical for denominator construction in incidence and prevalence studies.

CDISC standard for organising the raw clinical trial data submitted to FDA and PMDA. Each trial domain (DM, AE, LB, EX) maps to a defined SDTM table with prescribed variables and controlled terminology.

CDISC standard for the analysis-ready datasets that support a clinical trial's statistical analysis plan. Built from SDTM with traceability variables; ADSL (subject-level) is the foundation for all efficacy and safety ADaM datasets.

CDISC machine-readable metadata document submitted alongside SDTM/ADaM data. Describes datasets, variables, controlled terminology, and value-level metadata so reviewers can validate the submission programmatically.
CDISC XML standard for capturing and exchanging clinical trial case report form data and metadata between EDC systems, sponsors, and regulators. Preserves audit trails and electronic signatures.
ICH-maintained terminology for adverse event coding in pharmacovigilance and clinical trials. Five-level hierarchy from System Organ Class down to Lowest Level Term.
The MedDRA hierarchy level used as the unit of analysis for safety reporting. AEs reported by sites at the verbatim level are mapped to a Preferred Term during medical coding.
SDTM variable carrying a study-wide unique subject identifier, typically formed by concatenating study, site, and subject id. The join key for almost every cross-domain SDTM and ADaM operation.

Legacy fixed-position binary file format that FDA and PMDA require for SDTM and ADaM submission. Variable names are limited to 8 characters and labels to 40 characters, which constrains CDISC variable naming.
JSON object an exchange sends to bidders inviting them to bid on a single impression opportunity. Carries imp, site/app, device, user, and regs blocks per the OpenRTB specification.
The minimum CPM a publisher will accept for an impression, set per imp in the OpenRTB BidRequest. Hard floors filter bids below the threshold; soft floors are advisory in second-price auctions.

A publisher-side technique that solicits bids from multiple SSPs in parallel before the ad server's waterfall, increasing competition for each impression. Implemented client-side via Prebid.js or server-side via PBS.
Programmatic auction model in which each impression is sold individually via a sub-100ms auction across many bidders. The dominant transaction shape on most open exchanges.

Pre-negotiated programmatic deals between specific buyers and sellers, executed over the OpenRTB rails but with deal_id-scoped pricing and inventory. Includes Preferred Deals, PMPs, and Programmatic Guaranteed.

An IAB Tech Lab plaintext file at /ads.txt on a publisher's domain listing the sellers and seller account ids authorised to sell its inventory. Buyers reject bids from unauthorised sellers to combat domain spoofing.
Companion to ads.txt — a JSON file an SSP hosts at /sellers.json declaring every seller it represents. Lets buyers verify the supply chain end-to-end via the SupplyChain Object in OpenRTB.

IAB Tech Lab specification for in-app and in-web ad measurement that lets a single SDK report viewability and verification signals to many measurement vendors without each requiring its own integration.
Share of served impressions that meet the MRC viewability standard — at least 50% of pixels on screen for at least one second for display, two seconds for video.

Ad traffic that does not represent real user interest. General IVT (GIVT) is filtered with declared bot lists; Sophisticated IVT (SIVT) requires behavioural detection and includes hijacked devices and bot farms.

IAB Europe framework for collecting and signalling user consent under GDPR, encoded in a Consent String passed through the OpenRTB User Ext. v2.2 added explicit purpose disclosures and cleaner legitimate-interest handling.

IAB Tech Lab successor signalling format that combines TCF, U.S. State, and other regional consent strings into a single header-bearable string. Designed to scale to new privacy jurisdictions without re-plumbing.

IAB Tech Lab object model that factors out shared types (placement, creative, context) used by OpenRTB, OpenDirect, and adCOM consumers. Versioned independently of OpenRTB to allow separate evolution.

Open Charge Alliance protocol between EV chargers (Charge Points) and their backend (Central System / CSMS). Versions 1.6 (SOAP/JSON) and 2.0.1 (JSON over WebSocket with security profiles) are the deployed baselines.

EV roaming protocol between charge point operators (CPOs) and e-mobility service providers (EMSPs). Standardises Locations, Tariffs, Sessions, and CDR exchange so a driver can roam across networks with a single subscription.
Pricing schedule a charging session is billed against — combining time, energy, and parking components, often with time-of-use bands. Carried in OCPI as a Tariff object referenced from each session.

ISO standard for communication between an EV and a charging station, including high-level protocol stacks for AC and DC charging. Underpins Plug-and-Charge identification and bi-directional energy transfer.
ISO 15118 capability that lets a driver authorise and pay for a charging session purely by plugging in — the vehicle and charger exchange certificates without a card tap or app interaction.
Bi-directional charging that allows an EV battery to discharge to the grid during peak demand under a utility's V2G program. Requires ISO 15118 -20 and bi-directional onboard or DC chargers.
OCPP message a charge point sends periodically during a transaction reporting energy.active.import.register, current, voltage, and other sampled values. The audit trail behind every kWh billed.

OCPP 1.6 message (TransactionEvent in 2.0.1) a charge point sends when a session begins, carrying connectorId, idTag, meterStart, and timestamp. Pairs with StopTransaction at session end to bound a billable charging session.

Card or fob a driver presents at a charge point to authenticate a charging session in lieu of an app or Plug-and-Charge. Identified by an idTag string sent in OCPP Authorize and StartTransaction messages.

FOCUS column representing the cost a cloud provider invoices for a charge in the billing period, after commitment-based discounts and credits are applied. The number that reconciles to the customer's invoice.

FOCUS column representing the amortised cost of a charge after spreading commitment fees across the term they cover. Used for unit-economics comparisons that need consistent treatment across reservation purchases.
FOCUS column representing the cost of a charge at the publicly listed on-demand price, before commitment, negotiated, or volume discounts. Useful for measuring discount yield versus list.
A pricing construct in which a customer commits to a baseline of usage in exchange for a discount versus on-demand. FOCUS represents these via CommitmentDiscountId, Type, and Status columns.
A key-value label attached to a cloud resource for cost allocation, ownership, or environment tracking. FOCUS surfaces tags via the Tags column as a JSON-encoded map for analytic querying.
FOCUS controlled-vocabulary value that buckets each charge into a high-level cloud service group (Compute, Storage, AI and Machine Learning, Networking, etc.) for cross-provider comparison.
FOCUS column expressing the unit a charge is priced in — vCPU-Hours, GB-Months, Requests. Lets analytics aggregate quantities across providers without conflating heterogeneous units.
FOCUS pair of columns (ChargePeriodStart, ChargePeriodEnd) bounding the time window a charge applies to. Foundational for accurate amortisation and commitment-coverage analytics.

ISO 20022 securities settlement instruction message used by an account owner to instruct its custodian on a delivery or receipt of securities. Carries trade details, settlement parties, and SD/SD+1 instructions.
ISO 20022 securities post-trade message a custodian sends to report transaction postings on a securities account. Anchors break investigations and reconciliation against trade-side records.
Field on a securities settlement instruction reporting whether the CSD has paired the instruction with the counterparty's matching instruction. Unmatched and mismatched are the two failure states.
12-character ISO 6166 identifier for a security — country code, NSIN, and check digit. The dominant cross-border instrument identifier used in settlement, custody, and regulatory reporting.
ISO 9362 8- or 11-character code identifying a financial institution and optionally a branch. Used to address SWIFT MT and ISO 20022 messages and to identify settlement parties in CSD instructions.

ISO 17442 20-character identifier for a legal entity participating in financial transactions. Mandated by EMIR, MiFID II, and Dodd-Frank for transaction-level reporting; issued by Local Operating Units.

ISO 10962 6-character code classifying an instrument by category, group, and attributes. Required alongside ISIN for MiFID II transaction reporting and helps disambiguate equity classes and bond seniority.

EU regulation that governs CSDs and securities settlement, including the Settlement Discipline Regime that imposes cash penalties for late or failed settlements and mandates buy-ins for persistent fails.
Settlement cycle in which trades settle on the business day following the trade date. The U.S., Canada, and Mexico moved to T+1 in May 2024; the EU and UK have committed to follow in October 2027.
A CSDR-mandated procedure in which a failing seller's broker is forced to source the securities in the open market to deliver to the buyer, with the original seller covering any price difference.

A lender's instruction calling back loaned securities — typically because the underlying owner has sold or wishes to vote a corporate action. Failure to return on time can trigger a buy-in under CSDR.

IRS XML-based platform for electronic filing of federal tax returns. Replaced the legacy EMS system; supports business and individual returns with real-time acknowledgements and structured error feedback.
The U.S. individual federal income tax return. Schedules attach to address specific income types, deductions, and credits beyond the main return.
The federal income tax return for U.S. C corporations, including subsidiary forms 1120-S (S corporations), 1120-F (foreign corporations), and 1120-L (life insurance companies).
The federal return for partnerships and LLCs taxed as partnerships. Schedule K-1 flows through to each partner's individual or entity return.

Supplemental form that attaches to a base IRS return to detail a category of income, deduction, or credit (e.g. Schedule A itemised deductions, Schedule C self-employment, Schedule K-1 partner income).

An MeF response message confirming the IRS's receipt of an e-filed return and reporting whether it was Accepted or Rejected with a list of validation errors. Logged into MeF audit trails per submission.
U.S. statute requiring foreign financial institutions to report on accounts held by U.S. persons, enforced via withholding on non-compliant payments. Reported on Forms 8966, 1042, and 1042-S.

OECD standard for automatic exchange of financial account information between participating jurisdictions. Functions as the international counterpart to FATCA and is implemented via local CRS reporting forms.

Mechanism by which a payer remits a portion of a payment directly to a tax authority on behalf of the payee. U.S. examples include W-2 wage withholding, 1042 nonresident withholding, and backup withholding.

Gross income minus above-the-line adjustments (educator expenses, HSA contributions, student loan interest, etc.). Drives eligibility for many tax credits, IRA deduction limits, and Medicare premium tiers.

Parallel federal tax computation that disallows certain preferences, deductions, and credits. Filers pay the higher of regular tax and AMT; corporate AMT was reintroduced under the 2022 IRA at a 15% book-income floor.
System-generated, source-independent integer or hash key used as the primary identifier of a dimension or fact row. Decouples the warehouse from upstream identifier changes and supports SCD2 history.
The identifier a business uses for an entity in its source system — a customer number, ISIN, NPI. Stored alongside the surrogate key but never used as the join key in the dimensional model.

Data Vault 2.0 modeling pattern. Hubs hold business keys, Links capture relationships between Hubs, and Satellites carry descriptive attributes with effective dates, enabling auditable, parallel-loadable warehouses.
A hash of a row's descriptive attributes used to detect change cheaply during ETL. In Data Vault Satellites, a new row is inserted only when the hash differs from the most recent active row.

A dimension shared across multiple fact tables with identical structure and meaning, enabling drill-across analysis. Conformed Date, Customer, and Product dimensions are the backbone of bus-architecture warehouses.

A table that resolves many-to-many relationships between a fact and a dimension — for example, a household membership bridge between an account fact and a customer dimension. Often carries a weighting factor for fair allocation.
The exact level of detail a fact row represents — one transaction, one daily snapshot, one claim line. Defining the grain is the first step in dimensional design and should never silently change.

A dimension row that arrives after a fact references it. Handled by inserting a placeholder dimension row at fact-load time and back-filling the descriptive attributes when the dimension feed catches up.

Open protocol (Google + Visa + Mastercard + Amex et al.) that defines IntentMandate, CartMandate, and PaymentMandate as signed payloads carrying agent-initiated purchase authority through the payments stack. Includes carry-back of disputes to agent operators.
JSON-RPC 2.0 contract published by Anthropic for connecting LLM agents to external tools, resources, and prompts. Implemented by Stripe, Shopify, Square, PayPal MCP servers among others.

Network-issued identifier (Visa Trusted Agent Protocol / Mastercard Agent Pay) that uniquely identifies a transacting agent across operators. Carried in the auth message via the Visa AGI / Mastercard AAI flag.
The signed chain of authority from principal → operator → agent → merchant that proves an agent's transaction was legitimately authorized. Verified at AP2 PaymentMandate evaluation time.
Signed declaration of what the principal wants the agent to accomplish (budget, deadline, category). The grain at which agentic-conversion attribution is computed.
Out-of-band re-authentication of the human principal via WebAuthn or W3C Secure Payment Confirmation when an agent transaction crosses a risk-threshold (amount, new merchant, anomalous geography).
A single JSON-RPC 2.0 method invocation an agent sends to an MCP server (e.g. search_products, create_cart, payment_intent.create). Recorded for trace, billing, and audit.
A purchase whose attribution chain terminates at an agent's IntentMandate rather than a click on a marketing surface. Multi-touch credit assignment must operate at intent grain.
The signed transfer of a built CartMandate from agent to principal for one-tap confirmation, or from one agent to another agent (cross-platform).
Cryptographic binding of a tokenized payment instrument to a specific agent + grant + merchant tuple, so a stolen token cannot be replayed in a different context.
OAuth 2.0 extension (RFC 9396) that lets an authorization request carry structured authorization_details (amount caps, merchant scope, expiry). The protocol substrate AP2 IntentMandates ride on.
Composite trust index for an agent derived from operator attestation, behavioral history, dispute rate, and cross-network signals (Skyfire, Visa KYA, Mastercard AAI).
A non-buying agent on the other side of an agent-to-agent interaction — typically a merchant-side concierge or negotiator. Both sides require KYA and signed delegation.
Human user on whose behalf an agent acts. Remains the cardholder of record for all dispute and refund purposes.
An agent that holds a delegation token by virtue of possession (analogous to a bearer instrument). Risky relative to attested agents and typically capped at low amounts.
AP2 payload signed by the principal expressing what they want done. First node in the AP2 mandate chain.
AP2 payload built by the agent and presented to the principal for one-tap confirmation. Contains line items, totals, merchant — signed for non-repudiation.
AP2 payload that authorizes the actual debit. References the CartMandate and IntentMandate; its signature is the substrate networks check before authorization.

Monthly cross-functional process that reconciles demand, supply, finance, and product plans into one consensus number set per Oliver Wight's five-step cycle (Product Review → Demand Review → Supply Review → Integrated Reconciliation → MBR).
Evolved S&OP that integrates financial outcomes, strategic initiatives, and scenario planning. Operated as a connected planning canvas across SAP IBP, Kinaxis, o9, Anaplan and similar.
Forecast accuracy metric — mean of absolute(actual − forecast) / actual across rows. Penalizes percentage error uniformly, breaks down when actual is near zero.
Weighted accuracy metric — sum of absolute errors divided by sum of actuals. Robust to near-zero actuals; preferred in retail and CPG.
Systematic over- or under-forecast. Computed as sum(forecast − actual) / sum(actual); should oscillate around zero. Persistent positive bias drives excess inventory; negative bias drives stockouts.
Order is delivered both on the requested date and complete — no shorts, no late lines. The headline service-level metric the supply plan defends.
Inventory measured in days of forward demand. Computed as avg_inventory_units / avg_daily_demand_units. Targeted per ABC class — A items low DOH, C items higher.
Percentage of order lines (or cases) shipped complete on first pass. Different from OTIF in that fill ignores the on-time component.
Short-horizon (days–weeks) forecast refinement driven by near-real-time signals — POS, sell-through, weather, web demand, channel inventory. Distinct from statistical baseline.
Active influence on demand through pricing, promotion, allocation, or channel routing to align with available supply.
The single, signed-off demand number set produced by Integrated Reconciliation. All commercial + finance + supply teams plan against this number.
Third step in Oliver Wight five-step. Net-supply the demand consensus against capacity, inventory, lead-times; surface the supply-demand gaps.
The fifth and final step — exec sign-off on the consensus plan, gap-to-budget, and required interventions. Often chaired by COO / CSCO.

A named alternate plan — supply disruption, demand surge, tariff shock — evaluated against the base plan for revenue, working capital, and service-level impact. Kinaxis / SAP IBP / o9 are scenario-first systems.
Joint optimization of safety stock across plant → DC → forward-DC → store tiers, recognising that pooling at higher tiers reduces total network inventory for the same service level.
Resource-period combination where planned load exceeds available capacity. Propagated through the BOM and network by a finite-capacity solver.
The canonical SKU × stocking-location grain at which most supply chain plans, inventory positions, and accuracy metrics are calculated.
Plan expressed as quantities per period (day / week / month) over a rolling horizon — typically 18-36 months for IBP. Contrasted with single-number annual budgets.
Decision rule for batching production / purchase orders — economic order quantity (EOQ), fixed lot, period order quantity, Wagner-Whitin, etc.

Difference between book inventory and physical inventory, expressed in dollars or as a percentage of net sales. Comprises theft (internal + external + ORC), administrative error, vendor fraud, and damage.
Portion of shrink with a documented root cause and a closed case in the LP investigation system. Counter to "unknown shrink".
Residual shrink at period close that lacks a documented cause. Usually external theft + administrative error. Converting unknown to known is the LP program's leading indicator.

Cashier-level loss pattern where the associate undercharges or fails to charge friends/family — often via voided lines, fake discounts, or barcode-swap on premium SKUs. Detected via NCR Voyix LP / Oracle XBR / Profitect rule engines.

Coordinated theft operations — boost-and-fence rings that steal high-CRAVED merchandise across multiple stores and resell through marketplaces or pawn networks. Tracked across chains via Auror and shared with law enforcement via ALTO Alliance.
Fraudulent return — no-receipt return of stolen goods, swapped-content return (rocks for electronics), or refund-to-fresh-card scheme. Scored at counter via Appriss Retail Verify.
Policy abuse — wearing the apparel before returning, returning beyond the published window, or repeated returns that abuse a generous policy without crossing into outright fraud.
Hard-tag or soft-tag system (Sensormatic AM 58 kHz, Checkpoint RF) that triggers a pedestal alarm on unsecured exit. Combined with item-level RFID in modern stores for inventory accuracy.
Clarke's mnemonic for high-theft items — Concealable, Removable, Available, Valuable, Enjoyable, Disposable. Drives where EAS / RFID / Indyme smart locks get deployed.

Detected POS-side anomaly — high-value refund, void-after-tender, suspicious price override, barcode swap, cash skim. The exception engines (NCR Voyix LP, Oracle XBR, Profitect, Aptos LP, Datalogic lane-awareness, Honeywell HCI) all produce a stream of these.
Cashier voids a tendered transaction after cash is collected — pocketing the cash and leaving the till balanced. A leading sweethearting/internal-theft signal.
Drawer opened without a sale recorded. Sometimes legitimate (change-making) — but frequency × duration of no-sale opens correlates with cash-skim.
Direct cash theft from the register — voided sales with cash kept, short-rung sales, or under-rung change. Detected by reconciling tender drops to system sales.
Modern umbrella term for the LP function, expanded to include safety, fraud, OSHA compliance, and supply-chain shrink — not just floor theft.
An intermediary buyer who knowingly purchases stolen goods from boosters and resells them through pawn shops or online marketplaces. ORC investigation targets the fence as much as the booster.
ORC slang for stealing (boost) and the person who steals (booster). A boost crew typically targets high-CRAVED SKUs across multiple stores in a single sweep.
The investigator's process of stitching exceptions, CCTV, witness statements, employee schedules, and recovered evidence into a packet for prosecution or civil demand.
Referral of a case to law enforcement for criminal prosecution. Typically reserved for cases above a felony threshold (state-specific) and where evidence is prosecution-grade.
Tamper-evident audit trail proving evidence (video, receipts, statements) hasn't been altered between collection and trial. Required by ASIS Asset Protection Standards and by most prosecutors.

Industry consortium and information-sharing standard that lets retailers and law-enforcement exchange case packets on ORC suspects, vehicles, and rings — under a tightly scoped multi-retailer disclosure framework.

Model-estimated time (in hours, cycles, or distance) an asset can continue to operate before reaching a defined failure or end-of-useful-life threshold. Canonical benchmarks defined by the NASA C-MAPSS turbofan dataset.
Average operating time between two consecutive failures on the same asset class. The headline reliability index for repairable equipment; complement to MTTF for non-repairable.
Average elapsed time from failure-event start to restored-to-service. Combines diagnosis, parts logistics, repair, and re-commissioning time.

Maintenance triggered by an observed condition (sensor crossing a threshold, vibration severity zone change) rather than fixed-interval calendar or runtime. Bridge between time-based PM and full predictive maintenance.

PdM extended to recommend a specific action (lubricate, align, replace bearing, derate) keyed to the predicted failure mode. AspenTech Mtell and Augury's recommendation engine are reference implementations.
Top-down deductive analysis tracing a system failure to its contributing component failures via Boolean gate logic. Backbone of IEC 61508 functional-safety quantification.
Systematic catalog of each component's possible failure modes, their effects, severity, occurrence, detection, and resulting risk priority number (RPN). Required input to the failure_mode taxonomy.

Characteristic vibration frequencies generated by rolling-element bearing defects — Ball Pass Frequency Outer race (BPFO), Inner race (BPFI), Ball Spin Frequency (BSF), Fundamental Train (cage) Frequency (FTF). Tones appear at integer multiples of shaft RPM.

RCM concept (SAE JA1011) — the interval from when a developing failure first becomes detectable (P) to when it manifests as functional failure (F). Defines the operational lead-time window in which intervention is possible.

The bridge between plant-floor control systems (PLC, SCADA, DCS) and enterprise data platforms. Demarcated by the Purdue Model L0–L4 zones; bridged by OPC UA aggregating servers and IEC 62443-classified DMZs.
Vendor-neutral industrial protocol for secure transport of machine data — typed information models, PKI-mutual-TLS auth, sub-second time-series. The default OT-IT bridge in greenfield plants.
Lightweight publish/subscribe protocol over TCP/TLS. The de-facto choice for retrofit wireless sensors and edge-to-cloud telemetry. Sparkplug B layers asset-aware payload conventions on top.

Software layer that aggregates real-time data from PLCs across a plant and provides operator HMI screens, alarms, and historian feeds. Common SCADA: Wonderware (Aveva System Platform), Rockwell FactoryTalk View, Siemens WinCC.

Industrial computer that executes ladder logic or function-block code at deterministic scan rates (typically 10–100ms) to control discrete or continuous plant equipment. Vendors: Siemens (SIMATIC S7), Rockwell (ControlLogix), Mitsubishi, Schneider.

Specialized database optimized for high-rate process tag time-series — typically year-decades of retention with compression. OSIsoft PI (now AVEVA PI System), Proficy Historian, Honeywell PHD are canonical.

Subset of historical operating data labeled as "known-good" for unsupervised anomaly detector training. Selecting the golden window is one of the highest-leverage modeling decisions — too narrow and the model is brittle; too wide and it learns the failure as normal.

Anomaly detection technique using a neural autoencoder trained on the golden window — at inference, samples with high reconstruction error are flagged. Robust for unsupervised PdM where labels are sparse.

Conversion of a time-domain vibration or acoustic signal into its frequency components. The basis tool for identifying bearing fault tones, gear mesh harmonics, and electrical line-frequency artifacts.

Fourth-moment statistic of a vibration signal; sensitive to impulsive content. Spikes in kurtosis are an early indicator of bearing damage (impacts at the fault frequency) before broad-band RMS rises.

Standardized assessment of overall machine vibration health using RMS velocity bands and Zone A/B/C/D thresholds keyed to machine class and rigid/flexible-mounting. ISO 20816 is the 2016 update to ISO 10816.

SKU on which shoppers form their price perception of the retailer — typically a high-frequency, high-traffic item whose price is checked across competitors. KVIs drive the Competitive Price Index and are protected from over-pricing.
Category whose pricing perception disproportionately drives store-choice — e.g. milk, bananas, soda. Category-level price guardrails apply rather than SKU-level.
The non-promotional ticketed price of a SKU at a store or price zone, governed by the regular-price line and EDI 832/879 cycles.
Temporary price during an active promotion. Carries a mechanic (% off, BOGO, multibuy) and a funded duration; falls back to regular at end.
Reduction of the regular price for a lifecycle-driven reason (excess inventory, seasonal end, clearance). Distinct from a promo because it is not time-boxed back to the original price.

Percentage of post-event volume above the no-promo statistical baseline. lift_pct = (actual_units − baseline_units) / baseline_units. Headline measurement of promo effectiveness; should be reported net of cannibalization and halo.
Sales transferred from a related SKU's baseline to the promoted SKU. Naive lift over-credits when cannibalization is not subtracted; commonly 5–30% of headline lift on hero promotions.
Incremental sales of complementary SKUs caused by a promotion on another SKU (e.g. burger promo lifts bun sales). Counted opposite to cannibalization in net-lift measurement.
Percentage change in units sold per 1% change in price (negative number for normal goods). Estimated per cluster (SKU × store cluster × time window).
Pricing strategy in which the retailer offers consistently low prices on most items rather than running deep promotions. Walmart and Aldi are exemplars.
Pricing strategy in which regular prices sit above EDLP equivalents but frequent deep promotions create traffic and basket-build. Common at Kroger, Albertsons, Carrefour.
Forward-looking schedule of promotions by category × week, used to coordinate inventory, ads, and vendor funding. Conflicts between categories trigger clearance reviews.
Ordered price points across a brand/pack hierarchy designed to steer shoppers among entry, mainstream, and premium tiers without leaving margin or volume on the table.
Combination of pack sizes and price points across a portfolio (e.g. single, 6-pack, 12-pack, 24-pack) tuned to channel occasions and willingness-to-pay.
Share of in-store and online price observations where the realized price matches the planned regular/promo price. Drift comes from late tag changes, POS overrides, and feed timing.
Counterfactual margin lost by setting markdown depth or timing sub-optimally vs the optimizer's recommendation. Tracks the cost of category-manager overrides.

Money a CPG manufacturer commits to a retailer to fund promotional pricing, displays, features, slotting, and pay-for-performance. Globally >$1T/yr; second-largest line item after COGS for most CPG firms.
Share of received units actually sold within a window. Drives markdown timing — low sell-through with a fixed end-of-season deadline triggers deeper-and-earlier markdowns.

Manufacturer-funded credit issued via a chargeback to a wholesaler or retailer that resold an item at an agreed contract price below the standard wholesale list. The pool covers the per-unit difference; the manufacturer reconciles by claim line.

Trade-promotion settlement method in which the retailer ships at full price and "bills back" the manufacturer after performance is verified. Creates AR exposure and longer cash cycles than off-invoice but allows pay-for-performance gating.

Trade-promotion settlement method in which the manufacturer credits the retailer for each promoted unit actually scanned at point-of-sale during the promo window. Reconciled from EDI 852 / Circana / NielsenIQ scan feeds.

Trade-promotion settlement method in which the discount is applied as a per-case allowance directly on the manufacturer's invoice at ship time. Fastest cash treatment but creates forward-buy exposure and no enforceable performance gate.

Statistical estimate of what would have sold without any promotion in a given week. Computed by Circana Unify, NielsenIQ baseline, T-Pro Predictive, or in-house GLM/ML; the choice of model materially changes reported ROI.
Units sold above baseline during a promo period. The numerator of lift and the denominator-driver for promo ROI; defended in syndicated audits (Circana, NielsenIQ, Numerator).

Retailer's deliberate ordering of additional inventory during a promo window to lock in the discount and drain shelves at full price afterwards. Inflates short-term shipments and depresses post-promo baseline; the classic source of bullwhip in CPG.
Incremental sales of related (non-promoted) SKUs caused by traffic / basket-build from a promoted SKU. Counted opposite cannibalization in net-incremental measurement.

Composite retail-execution KPI combining distribution, share of shelf, planogram compliance, price compliance, and promo compliance for a single outlet. Coca-Cola, Unilever, and PepsiCo publish branded scoring frameworks.

The set of in-store activities — display set-up, shelf restocking, planogram audit, price-tag verification, promo compliance — that bridge the planned promo and the shopper. AFS Retail Execution and Salesforce Consumer Goods Cloud are reference platforms.

Manufacturer-set price floor below which a retailer may not advertise (in-store sign, circular, online listing). Distinct from MSRP because it governs advertising not the actual transacted price; enforced via co-op funding and term sheets.
ASC X12 EDI transaction set carrying weekly POS movement and on-hand inventory from retailer to manufacturer. The early-signal feed for in-flight promo monitoring; coverage varies by retailer.
ASC X12 EDI transaction set reporting product movement and resale to consumer. Used to verify scan-down claims and reconcile sell-through; complements EDI 852.
NRF-led standards body publishing trade-promo data interchange profiles (promotion plan, tactic, settlement evidence). Adoption is patchy but reduces vendor-specific connector cost when present.
aliases: Association for Retail Open Trading Standards

extras.definition: Trade-spend funding model in which committed funds are released only on verified compliance evidence — display photo audit, scan-flag, retail-execution visit log. Reduces trade rate but adds reconciliation overhead.

Annual collaborative plan between manufacturer and retailer covering volume targets, trade spend, innovation rollouts, and operational metrics. The retailer score-card rolls into the JBP review at quarterly checkpoints.

System that unifies first-party customer data from multiple sources, resolves identity, and exposes audiences to activation destinations. Canonical vendors include Salesforce Data Cloud, Adobe RT-CDP, Treasure Data, mParticle, Tealium AudienceStream, Twilio Segment, and Amperity.
System that manages customer-facing interactions and account history — Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, HubSpot. The CDP feeds CRM; the CRM is rarely the system of record for behavioral events.

Set of edges connecting observed identifiers (hashed email, hashed phone, device IDs, ad IDs, loyalty IDs, cookies) to a single resolved customer_master. Built by deterministic + probabilistic stitching.
Identity merge based on a shared, high-confidence identifier (e.g. authenticated login, hashed email, loyalty ID). Precision near 1.0; recall limited by anonymous traffic.

Identity merge based on inferred signals (IP, user-agent, behavioral patterns, postal proximity) above a tuned confidence threshold. Recall higher than deterministic; precision risks polluting golden records.
Single canonical customer record produced by survivorship rules across multiple source-system inputs. The row a personalization engine targets; the unit of CLV computation.

Behavioural segmentation scheme assigning each customer a 1-5 score on Recency (days since last purchase), Frequency (orders per period), and Monetary (spend per period). Produces 125 cells; high-RFM cells (4-5/4-5/4-5) are champions.
Customer-loyalty index computed as %promoters (score 9-10) − %detractors (0-6) on the "how likely are you to recommend us" survey. Ranges -100 to +100.
A rules-, RFM-, behavioural-, or model-defined group of customers eligible for a particular campaign / journey / activation destination. Refreshed on cadences from real-time to weekly.
Legally-defensible record of a customer's consent grant, withdrawal, or rights-request action. Stored alongside the IAB TCF v2.2 / GPP encoded consent string and the lawful basis under GDPR Art. 6.
Channel-and-topic preference state declaring whether a customer wants to receive a class of messages. Authoritative for send-eligibility checks; suppressions propagate to all destinations.
Discrete stage on the customer journey — prospect, new, active, lapsed, churned, reactivated, VIP — driving which journey treatments and which channels apply.
SHA-256 hash of a normalized identifier (lower-cased trimmed email, E.164 phone) — the PII-safe envelope every major destination (Meta CAPI, Google EUID, TikTok Events) accepts.
Policy that picks the winning attribute value when sources disagree (most-recent, highest-trust, longest-non-null, weighted vote). The mechanism by which the golden record is constructed and audited.
Qualitative archetype describing a customer cluster's motivations, channels, and content preferences. Built from segmentation outputs + research; consumed by marketing for creative direction.
Stratification of loyalty-program members by accumulated points or spend within a window — bronze, silver, gold, platinum, black, founder. Each tier carries benefits + earn multipliers.
Append-only book of record for every points credit and debit. Drives points-liability accounting under FASB ASC 606 deferred-revenue treatment.
Event where a customer trades loyalty points (or status) for a reward — gift card, voucher, discount, partner experience. Drives the redemption-rate KPI and points-liability draw-down.

Pattern of syncing modelled data from a cloud warehouse back to operational tools (Klaviyo, Braze, Iterable, Meta audiences) — typically via Hightouch, Census, or Segment Profile Sync. The activation half of the warehouse-native CDP architecture.

Sellable inventory at a node after subtracting allocated, in-transit-out, and reserved-safety quantities. The number a checkout cart can confidently promise the customer in real time. ATP refresh latency is the central engineering tradeoff in distributed OMS.

Service that quotes a delivery date / pickup time at checkout by combining sourcing-rule simulation, ATP, carrier transit times, and store pick capacity. Manhattan Active Promise and IBM Sterling Promise are reference implementations.

Fulfillment method where the customer purchases on .com / mobile and collects at a designated store. Reduces last-mile cost, drives store traffic, and shifts the SLA clock to "ready-for-pickup" rather than "delivered".

Reverse-logistics pattern where an online order is returned at a physical store. Reduces freight cost and creates an upsell opportunity at refund time. Accounts for 60-70% of online returns at omnichannel retailers.
Fulfillment of a .com order out of a store's on-hand inventory. Trades higher per-pick labor cost for shorter zone-skip transit + clearance pull on stranded inventory.
Mid-tier warehouse positioned regionally to compress last-mile transit; sits between national-scale fulfillment and local stores in the network design.

Outsourced model where the brand uses a third-party network (Shopify Fulfillment Network, ShipBob, Deliverr) for pick-pack-ship. The OMS routes through the partner's API contract rather than the brand's WMS.

Configurable rule fragments evaluated by the Distributed Order Management (DOM) broker to score candidate fulfillment nodes. Manhattan strategies, Sterling business-rules, Fluent GraphQL rules, and Salesforce OMS flows are vendor-specific dialects of the same idea.

Fulfillment method where the order is shipped directly from the vendor or supplier to the customer without ever entering the retailer's warehouse. Removes inventory carry; adds 1-2 days transit and reconciliation overhead.

ASC X12 EDI transaction pair for retailer-WMS coordination. EDI 940 instructs the WMS to ship; EDI 945 confirms what shipped, with serials, weights, and tracking. The two messages bracket the warehouse leg of the order lifecycle.

The orchestration layer of an OMS that decides which node fulfills which order line. Inputs are inventory positions across nodes, sourcing rules, capacity, carrier costs, and customer promise; outputs are allocations and ship-from decisions.

Single canonical customer record stitched across .com, store loyalty, and call-center identifiers. The unit of returns lookup, promo eligibility, and lifetime-value calculation; the OMS keys returns to the golden record so a BORIS lookup finds the original .com order.

The delivery-date interval quoted at checkout (e.g. "arrives Wed-Fri"). Tighter windows lift conversion but raise SLA-breach risk; the Order Promise Provider service derives the window from sourcing simulation + carrier ETAs + safety buffer.

In-store ordering capability where an associate can promise a SKU not on the rack from the chain's pool, fulfilling via ship-to-home or pickup-at-another-store. Aptos ONE and Manhattan POS are reference implementations.

A retail box converted to a pure fulfillment node — no retail traffic, full pick / pack labor — typically positioned in a high-density urban zone to compress last-mile time. Common in grocery (Walmart, Tesco) and apparel.
Variant of BOPIS where the staff brings the order to a customer's vehicle at a marked spot. Adds a customer-arrival signal to the lifecycle; common in grocery + general merch.

End-to-end flow of a returned product back through the network — drop-off, transit, inspection, restock-or-disposition, and refund. The mirror of forward fulfillment with its own KPIs and partner ecosystem (Happy Returns, Loop, Optoro).

The structured set of pack sizes, formats, and price points across a brand portfolio (entry / mainstream / premium / value / super tiers) that engineers consumer trade-up and trade-down within and across channels. The strategic centerpiece of CPG Revenue Growth Management.

The end-to-end commercial execution plan for a brand or portfolio — channel mix, pricing, trade investment, distribution, retail-execution. In RGM, GTM cost allocation (slotting, MDF, launch budgets) is the noisiest line in the gross-to-net waterfall.

Gross revenue minus all gross-to-net items (off-invoice, scan-down, bill-back, MCB, rebate accruals, slotting amortization, marketing development funds, returns). The post-trade top line that flows through to gross margin.

The structured ladder of deductions between gross sales (units × list price) and net revenue — off-invoice allowances, scan-downs, bill-backs, manufacturer chargebacks (MCB), rebate accruals, slotting fees, marketing development funds, returns. Governed by IFRS 15 variable-consideration accounting.
Ratio of net realized price to original list price, net of all trade deductions. Used interchangeably with price realization at the per-unit grain.
Net price divided by list price, weighted by units. Tracks how much of the published wholesale price actually lands in the manufacturer's books after the gross-to-net waterfall runs.
Change in the share of premium vs mainstream vs value packs (or channels) over a period. The dimension of variance that's hardest to attribute cleanly because it interacts with both volume and price.

A pack sized larger than the mainstream pack but priced below pro-rata to drive volume and household penetration (e.g. 18-count value pack vs the mainstream 12-count). Sits at the value tier of the PPA ladder.

A very large pack format (24-, 36-, 48-count) sold predominantly through club channels (Costco, Sam's Club, BJ's). High volume per scan, lower margin per unit; lives at the super tier of the PPA ladder.
Pack containing multiple individual selling units (e.g. 12-pack of soda, 6-pack of yogurt). The mainstream pack tier in most grocery categories.
The high-price, high-margin tier of the PPA ladder — typically smaller, more elaborate pack formats (single-serve glass, gift box, limited edition). The tier that drives Mix Index uplift.
The volume-anchor tier of the PPA ladder — the pack format with the largest share of category volume. Most distribution and promo investment concentrates here.
The price-tier where consumers entering the category or shopping on budget transact. The PPA tier where trade-down risk is highest and where channel ladder breakage hurts most.

The structured per-unit price differential maintained across club, mass, grocery, drug, convenience, and ecom channels. Breaking the ladder (e.g. a club exclusive at a lower per-unit) creates consumer perception arbitrage that's expensive to repair.
An up-front, fixed-amount trade payment to a retailer (vs accrual-based pay-per-unit). Higher cash exposure but simpler to administer; common for slotting fees and innovation launch programs.
A back-end rebate that only pays out if the retailer hits a performance threshold (volume, distribution coverage, display compliance). Replaces guaranteed off-invoice with pay-for-performance gating.

Period-end provision booked against expected future trade payouts (rebates, bill-backs, MCB) before they are formally claimed and settled. Under IFRS 15 it's the variable-consideration estimate inside net revenue.
Share of net revenue from SKUs launched in the trailing 24 months. Must be reported net of cannibalization on the existing portfolio or it over-credits the innovation pipeline.

Distribution model where a CPG manufacturer's truck delivers product directly from a depot to the retail store, bypassing the retailer DC. Dominant in beverage, snacks, beer, bakery, dairy; >$200B/yr in the US.
The end-to-end system of record for DSD operations — master routes, daily routes, settlement, returns, EPOD, driver pay. SAP DSD, Aldata Apollo, Epicor DSD, AFS DSD are reference platforms.
The recurring sequence of stops a route services on its standing service-day pattern (e.g. MWF). Re-cut quarterly as drop sizes and stop attrition shift.
One day's executed instance of a master route, with the optimized actual stop sequence after Roadnet/Descartes re-sequencing. The grain of stop, settlement, and EPOD records.
Average cases or units delivered per stop. The unit-economics input that flips a stop between deliver-mode and presell-mode (or off the route entirely).
DSD mode where an account sales rep visits the store today and writes an order for tomorrow's delivery truck. Decouples selling from delivery; preferred for high-value, low-frequency stops.
DSD mode where the same driver writes the order and delivers the product on the same visit. Faster cash but lower stop productivity than presell-and-deliver split.
On-handheld signature + photo + geo-stamp captured at the store door at delivery time. The single most important evidence artifact for disputing retailer chargebacks; carried inter-org by EDI 895.

End-of-day reconciliation of cash + check + EFT + returns + spoils between the driver and the cage. Variance triggers HR + finance review; high variance is one of the strongest fraud / shrink leading indicators.

Composite outlet-level retail-execution score — distribution, share-of-cooler, planogram, price, promo, freshness — captured by the driver/rep on the handheld at the visit. Drives pay-for-performance gating and trade-fund release.
Share of the contracted planogram's facings, blocks, and adjacencies actually present on the shelf at audit. The single biggest sub-score inside Perfect Store; gates pay-for-performance trade funds.
Share of authorized SKUs found in stock during a stop audit. The fast-feedback signal for cooler/shelf restock decisions and the trigger for off-cycle service visits.
An authorized SKU absent from the shelf or cooler during an audit. Mid-promo OOS silently destroys lift; in DSD it's correctable inside a single visit if the driver carries inventory on the truck.
Cases delivered as a share of cases ordered, at line grain. Industry benchmark 97-99%; below 95% triggers retailer chargebacks and lost-distribution risk.

Mid-day re-optimization of the remaining stop sequence on a route based on traffic, dwell-time overrun, or new orders. Trimble Roadnet, Descartes, Manhattan Active Routing all expose dynamic-routing APIs.
Inter-jurisdiction agreement governing fuel-tax allocation across U.S. states and Canadian provinces for commercial vehicles. Quarterly reporting requires precise GPS-to-jurisdiction mile splits.
GS1-issued unique identifier for a logistics unit (typically a pallet). Used to track DSD pallets from the depot bay through the truck to the store door.
A DSD transaction where the driver pulls expired/damaged product off the shelf and replaces it with fresh — modeled as a paired return + sale or a no-cash swap depending on the platform.
Product pulled from the shelf because it's past or near expiry. Credited to the retailer at settlement; a top driver of DSD returns rate.

Pre-loading of a DSD truck at the depot — each bay/slot mapped to a specific stop or product class to minimize at-store search time. Trimble Roadnet FleetLoader / MobileCast and Manhattan Active Routing publish bay-slot plans.
ASC X12 EDI transaction set carrying the manufacturer's DSD invoice (delivery or return) to the retailer at the door. Mirror to EDI 895 acknowledgment.
ASC X12 EDI transaction set carrying the retailer's signed acknowledgment of EDI 894 delivery + returns. The inter-org wire for EPOD evidence in deduction disputes.
Customer-facing authorization that an item may be sent back. Maps to EDI 180 between manufacturer and retailer. The header-grain object in returns analytics, with one or many return_items underneath.

Disposition where the refund is issued but the item is not requested back — economical when forward shipping + inspection + restock cost exceeds the unit recovery value. Pioneered at scale by Amazon and Walmart for low-cost categories.

A deduction from the refund issued to the customer to recover handling and inspection cost on a returned item. Capture rate (fees collected vs eligible) is a closely-tracked margin lever; high-friction in CX, often waived for loyalty tiers.

Restoring a returned item to a saleable state — cleaning, testing, repackaging, re-firmware-flashing, replacing consumables — through a Centralized Return Center (CRC). Yield (refurbed_A + refurbed_B share of inputs) drives net recovery vs liquidation.

Sale of unsellable-as-new returned product through secondary-market lot marketplaces (B-Stock, Liquidation.com, BULQ, Direct Liquidation, eBay B-Stock). Liquidation yield (proceeds / cost basis) sets the floor of return-flow economics.

The largest U.S. B2B liquidation-auction marketplace, where retailers and manufacturers sell off return-flow lots to vetted secondary-market buyers. Used as a generic noun for the channel itself ("send it to B-Stock").

Standard condition tiers assigned at the CRC. A-Grade = sellable as new, B-Grade = open-box with minor cosmetic, C-Grade = functional but not retail-presentable. Drives downstream routing — A back to restock, B to refurb channels, C to liquidation.

Elapsed time from RMA receipt to refund_issued. A CX-critical KPI — long refund times correlate strongly with churn and chargeback rates; targets vary by tender (instant-credit vs original-tender card).

The $700B+/yr global industry covering the flow of returned, recalled, refurbed, or recycled product back through the supply chain. Anchor vendors: Optoro, Loop Returns, Happy Returns (PayPal), Narvar, ZigZag, ReBound, Doddle, Newmine.

Omnichannel return method where a customer returns a .com order at a physical store of the same chain. Compresses the reverse leg (no carrier transit) and lifts attach-sale rate (~25% of BORIS visits add a new purchase).

A dedicated warehouse that inspects, grades, refurbs, and disposes returned product at scale. Most large retailers operate 1-3 CRCs; reverse-logistics 3PLs (Optoro, Newmine, GENCO/FedEx Supply Chain) operate shared-tenant CRCs.

Inventory model where common-return SKUs are held in forward DCs ready to resell — bypassing the round-trip to a CRC. Optoro OptiTurn and Happy Returns' aggregated-bag flow are leading patterns; lifts recovery value and compresses days-to-disposition.

Settlement model where the retailer pays the supplier only when the unit scans at POS — return ownership stays with the supplier. Heavy in newsstand and certain CPG categories; flips the returns risk allocation entirely.

Disposition pathway where a returned item is sent to a certified recycler rather than restocked, refurbed, or liquidated. Driven by EPR (Extended Producer Responsibility) regulation in EU and US states like California (SB 343).
Disposition pathway where unsellable-but-functional returned product is donated to a vetted charity (Good360, Delivering Good). Tax-deductible at fair market value; common for apparel and home goods.

Customer behavior where an item is bought, worn or used once, and returned for full refund. The most common form of "soft" return fraud; flagged by signal-based fraud platforms (Newmine, Appriss Retail) on patterns like rapid-return + tag-removed.

ASC X12 EDI transaction set carrying an RMA between trading partners. The B2B wire format that supplier returns portals and SAP S/4 Returns / Manhattan Returns emit; mirrors the customer-facing RMA in the OMS.

The authoritative shelf-layout document for a category × store-cluster × effective window — SKU placement, facings, shelf, slot, block adjacencies, vertical/horizontal flow. Authored in Blue Yonder Space Planning, Symphony RetailAI Category Manager, RELEX Space, or Quad Tag Galleria. The single instrument that converts category strategy into a store-executable artifact.
The set of SKUs a retailer authorises a category to carry across stores or per store-cluster. Range is the output of the range review; the planogram is the placement instance of the range.

The full SKU-by-store authorisation matrix for a category — which SKUs each store/cluster is permitted (or mandated) to carry. Distinct from range (banner-level) because the assortment matrix carries per-cluster differentiation.

ECR-blueprint category classification — Destination, Routine, Occasional/Seasonal, or Convenience — that drives shelf-space, pricing, promo intensity, and assortment-depth policy for a banner. Foundational input to the category business plan.

A category the retailer wants shoppers to choose its banner specifically for — gets the most shelf space, deepest assortment, sharpest price, and heaviest promo investment. Typically 5-10 categories per banner.
A category the retailer wants to be competitively viable on (price, range, in-stock) so that the trip basket completes there. Largest share of categories by count; competitive-parity assortment.
A category visited intermittently (BBQ, back-to-school, holiday) — disproportionate basket and margin contribution at peak; minimal shelf at trough. Range and planogram cycle seasonally.
A "fill-in" category not driving trip choice but supporting basket completion — narrow assortment, minimum space, no deep promo. Risk is over-investing space here at expense of Destination roles.

Ordered set of consumer-relevant attributes (flavor, pack, occasion, dietary, claim) the shopper uses to navigate a category. The structural input to assortment optimisation — must-stock walks the tree top-down to guarantee no branch is unstocked.

A brand's or SKU's share of a defined category × geography × time. Read from syndicated POS (Circana Unify / NielsenIQ Connect / Numerator) at value (dollars) and volume (units) cuts. The denominator definition (Total US Food vs Total US Multi-Outlet+) materially changes the number.
A manufacturer's aggregated share of a category across all its brands and sub-brands. Used for negotiating leverage in JBP (joint business planning) and for category-captain assignment.

Heuristic for allocating shelf space proportional to a brand's share of category sales — facings_brand ∝ share_brand × total_facings. Pure fair-share ignores margin, innovation, and shopper-loyalty signals; usually a constraint not an objective.

SKU whose absence creates loss-of-trip — the shopper walks to another banner if it's not on shelf. Identified by household-panel walk-away analysis (Kantar / Numerator) and shopper-insight studies; hard constraint in the assortment optimiser.

SKU recommended for removal in a range review — typically low velocity, low margin, low cannibalization-of-replacement. Velocity-only kill destroys halo on the brand; the right signal is decision-tree leaf coverage post-kill.

Three-tier SKU productivity ranking inside a category — Gold = top quintile (mandate + premium facings), Silver = mid (optional, cluster-restricted), Bronze = bottom (kill-candidate). Standard output of Symphony Category Manager and Circana Unify Assortment.

Multi-retailer, multi-brand panel and POS data licensed from a measurement provider (Circana, NielsenIQ, Numerator, Kantar Worldpanel, GfK). The truth source for cross-banner category share and competitive velocity benchmarking; the manufacturer does not own the raw retailer feed.

Census POS-scan feed (every transaction) aggregated weekly at SKU × store × week grain. Circana's MULO+ and NielsenIQ's Scantrack are reference cuts; basis for velocity, distribution, and price/promo elasticity computation.

A continuously-measured statistically-projected panel of households whose purchases (receipts, in-home scan, e-receipt) feed shopper-behaviour measurement — penetration, frequency, basket affinity, switching, walk-away. Numerator, NielsenIQ Homescan, Kantar Worldpanel are reference panels.
The top of the category hierarchy — the entire store assortment rolled up across all departments and categories. Anchor for cross-category share-of-wallet, halo, and trip-mission analytics.

The recurring (seasonal / annual) cycle in which retailer + manufacturer (often the Category Captain) jointly review velocity, share, margin, and cannibalization, then decide SKU adds, drops, mandates, repacks, and reclasses. Drives the next planogram cycle.

The single manufacturer (typically category leader) appointed by a retailer to advise on category strategy, range, and planogram across all manufacturers in the category. Privileged seat with regulatory antitrust guardrails (Robinson-Patman, FTC guidelines).

Grouping of stores sharing assortment policy — defined by demographic, shopper-mission, volume, or format axes. Replaces "one assortment for all stores"; typical retailer carries 4-8 clusters per category.

Share of the contracted planogram's facings, positions, and adjacencies actually present on the shelf at audit. Measured by image-recognition compliance audits (Trax, AFS, NIQ Audit, Numerator). Below 80% silently destroys range-review ROI.

Sum of All-Commodity-Volume weights of stores carrying an SKU divided by total ACV in the market. The standard industry metric for how widely an SKU is distributed; 80%+ ACV is the threshold for "broad national distribution."

Weekly units sold per store carrying the SKU — the rate at which the shelf turns. The single sharpest cut for SKU rationalisation; velocity index >1.0 vs category average is the threshold for "above-fair-share" facings.
GS1-issued lowest-level node of the Global Product Classification — globally consistent SKU classification (8-digit brick code). Used as the cross-supplier-cross-retailer category-hierarchy backbone.

Share of total addressable spend governed by an active contract or strategic sourcing event. Headline maturity KPI for the CPO; sub-65% means the procurement org isn't covering the long tail. Calculated as sum(spend_with_active_contract_or_strategic_sourced) / sum(total_spend).

Spend transacted outside negotiated contracts for a category the procurement org has covered. The leakage-detection metric — typically 5-20% of indirect spend; flagged by joining PO lines to active contract scope at ingest and surfaced on the maverick_flag column on po_line.

The bottom-80% of suppliers by spend, typically accounting for only ~5% of total spend but most of the supplier-count workload. Tackled via catalog/punchout consolidation, P-card programs, marketplace channels (Amazon Business, Tradeshift), or rule-driven auto-PO. Headline tail-spend ratio is a CPO KPI.

Corporate credit card issued for low-value, high-frequency purchases that bypass the requisition-PO-receipt-invoice flow. Trades AP workload for control loss; usage caps and category restrictions encoded at the issuer (Visa/Mastercard commercial card programs).

AP control that auto-clears an invoice only when PO, goods receipt, and supplier invoice agree on quantity, unit price, and amount within configured tolerance bands. Industry baseline for PO-backed invoice automation; tolerance is typically $50/2% per line.

Reduced match that compares only PO and invoice (no goods receipt). Used for services, subscription invoices, recurring fees, and low-value catalog spend where goods-receipt would cost more than the control gain.

Supplier invoice that flows from receipt through match through payment without human intervention. The headline AP automation KPI; world-class is >85% on PO-backed spend, ~60% on services. Pre-requisites are clean PO data, Peppol/EDI 810 receipt, and configured tolerance bands.

End-to-end procurement process from category strategy and supplier sourcing through contract, requisition, PO, receipt, invoice, and payment. The umbrella suite category (SAP Ariba, Coupa, Jaggaer, Ivalua, GEP SMART, Zycus). S2P replaced fragmented best-of-breed circa 2015.

The transactional subset of S2P — requisition through payment, excluding upstream sourcing/contracting. P2P optimization targets PO cycle time, touchless rates, three-way match coverage, and exception-resolution aging.

8-digit hierarchical category taxonomy (Segment-Family-Class-Commodity) maintained by GS1 US under license from the UN. Canonical key for spend cubing across multi-ERP enterprises; v26 carries ~150K commodity codes. Drives Scope 3 Category 1 attribution via spend-based emissions factors.
aliases: United Nations Standard Products and Services Code

extras.definition: Sourcing event where pre-qualified suppliers bid prices downward in a time-boxed window. Drives 5-15% price compression on commoditized categories with 4+ qualified bidders; ineffective for innovation/relationship spend or single-source items.

Three-stage sourcing instrument family — RFI for market discovery, RFP for solution-shaped responses with weighted scoring, RFQ for line-priced quotes against a fixed spec. eSourcing modules in Ariba Sourcing, Jaggaer ASO, Coupa Sourcing, Workday Strategic Sourcing (Scout).

WRI/WBCSD standard for indirect GHG emissions across 15 categories of an organization's value chain. Categories 1 (Purchased Goods & Services) and 2 (Capital Goods) are owned by the procurement org and reported under CSRD ESRS E1 and CDP. Attribution hierarchy is primary supplier data > activity-based factor > spend-based factor.

Supplier sustainability scorecard issued by EcoVadis on 0-100 scale across Environment / Labor & Human Rights / Ethics / Sustainable Procurement. Medals — Bronze ≥45, Silver ≥58, Gold ≥68, Platinum ≥78 (top 1%). Used as contract-eligibility floor; sustainable_spend_pct measures share of spend with Silver+ suppliers.

9-digit Dun & Bradstreet identifier assigned to every distinct business entity globally. The canonical join key for supplier deduplication across ERPs and S2P tools; parent_duns enables corporate-family roll-up so risk/sustainability scores attach to the parent while transactions flow against the local subsidiary.

Hard savings hit the P&L — negotiated unit-price drop on baseline volume with finance sign-off. Soft savings are cost avoidance (would-have-been increase deferred) or productivity gains tracked but not booked. Treat as separate columns on savings_event with explicit baseline_method and signed_off_by attribution.

Strategy of reducing the active supplier count in a category to concentrate spend on top performers — gains negotiated price, risk visibility, and Scope 3 data coverage at the cost of single-source exposure. Typical industrial program targets 30-60% supplier-count reduction over 18-24 months.

Buying integration where the buyer's S2P system launches the supplier's e-commerce site, the user shops, and the cart returns to the buyer's requisition as line items. cXML PunchOut is the dominant Ariba/Coupa protocol; OCI (Open Catalog Interface) is the SAP-flavored alternative.

Gap between contractually negotiated terms (price, rebate triggers, payment terms) and what actually transacts. Leakage shows up as price-list drift, missed rebate thresholds, off-contract spend, and payment terms not enforced at AP. Compounds at 0.5-2% of spend annually if unaddressed.

Pan-European e-invoicing standard built on UBL 2.1 + AS4 messaging over the Peppol network of access points. Mandatory for B2G invoicing in EU, expanding to B2B with the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) framework. Carried on invoice.peppol_message_id in the procurement model.

A place in the plant where equipment does a job, such as pump position 10-P-101A on a crude unit. It keeps its own history while the physical units installed in it are swapped, repaired and moved; joining the two by dated installations is what tells a bad position from a bad unit.

The standard code for how a piece of equipment failed (for example VIB vibration, ELP external leakage of process medium, FTS fail to start), from ISO 14224, the reliability-data standard for petroleum, petrochemical and natural gas equipment.
A multistage centrifugal pump with its motor, seal section, intake and power cable, run downhole to lift fluid from a well. The string is installed and pulled as one unit by a workover rig.

Days an ESP string runs in a well from start-up to failure or pull. Strings still running are censored observations, so run life is estimated with survival methods rather than a plain average of failed runs.

The teardown of a pulled ESP string to find why it failed, reported per API RP 11S1. Findings such as swollen seal elastomers or worn stages decide between a design change, a vendor claim and a well-condition fix.
Bringing a rig onto a producing well to pull and replace downhole equipment such as an ESP string. Rig availability often sets how long a failed well stays shut in.
A survival-curve estimate that uses units still running (censored) as well as failed ones. The median of the curve is the usual run-life figure for ESPs and pumps.
